channel.title: Microsoft Foundry on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in Microsoft Foundry on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: ai: From single call to agents: five new Claude capabilities now available in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now supports five new Claude capabilities on Azure-hosted models: structured outputs, web search, web fetch, MCP connector, and tool search. The update positions a model endpoint for agent-style workflows rather than single-call usage.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Azure Content Understanding GPT-5 Series Guide: Model Selection, Grounding Improvements, and Confidence Enhancements
item.description:
Azure Content Understanding is adding support for the GPT-5 series and updating grounding and confidence features. The change is intended to improve model selection flexibility, efficiency, and extraction quality across document, image, audio, and video content.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Building Agents that Act on Your Behalf with Toolboxes in Foundry
item.description:
Toolboxes in Microsoft Foundry are presented as a way to let agents act on a user’s behalf while handling delegated identity across tools and services. The post highlights using a private Entra-protected MCP server alongside Microsoft’s managed Work IQ MCP server in the same agent flow.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Protect sensitive generative AI telemetry in Application Insights and Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Application Insights now stores generative AI content in a dedicated GenAIContent table (AppGenAIContent in Log Analytics), enabling access controls for sensitive AI telemetry. The update is in public preview.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Announcing: Multi-agent orchestration SDK with the Microsoft Foundry Agent Framework in C# and Python
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry has introduced Agent Framework, a unified multi-agent orchestration SDK for C# and Python. It consolidates orchestration patterns previously split across AutoGen and Semantic Kernel into a single set of abstractions.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Announcing: Tracing for Microsoft Agent Framework (Python and .NET)
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now provides public preview tracing support for Microsoft Agent Framework in Python and .NET. The feature lets developers observe agent reasoning, tool calls, and model interactions during execution.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Open AI GPT-5.6 on Azure Databricks
item.description:
OpenAI GPT-5.6 is now generally available on Azure Databricks. Customers can use GPT 5.6 purchased through Microsoft Foundry via a Model Serving Endpoint in Azure Databricks.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: ai: What’s New in Microsoft Foundry | June 2026
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry’s June 2026 update adds Claude GA and several agent-related features released between Build 2026 and the end of June. It also calls out autopilot agents, expanded Toolboxes and Routines, and Agent Optimizer entering private preview.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Toolboxes in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry Toolboxes are now generally available. They provide a unified endpoint for commonly used tools in prompt agents and can also be invoked outside prompt agents.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: ai: Outcome-driven learning systems: Enterprise RL with OpenEnv and Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft says its Build 2026 Foundry releases fit together as an outcome-driven learning system for enterprise reinforcement learning, centered on OpenEnv and Foundry. The post positions hosted agents, Toolboxes, Foundry IQ, Memory, Managed Compute, fine-tuning, Frontier Tuning, and a new evaluation/optimization stack as supporting pieces of that system.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Microsoft Foundry agent security capabilities in Microsoft Defender for Cloud are transitioning to a Microsoft Agent 365 license
item.description:
Starting July 1, 2026, Microsoft Foundry agent security capabilities in Microsoft Defender for Cloud will move to a Microsoft Agent 365 license. Agent protection in Defender will use Agent 365 observability logs.

  • Source: Azure Updates
